quizName: DMV Practice Test #8 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Before carrying a passenger in traffic for the first time, you should:

options.text: Practice riding on a quiet road.
Flash your lights so others can see you.
Practice riding on the shoulder of a road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice riding on a quiet road.
questions.explanation: Before carrying a passenger in traffic for the first time, practice on a quiet road. This helps you get used to how your motorcycle handles with the extra weight.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white backgrounds and black letters or symbols. You must follow the speed limits shown on these signs.

questions.question: When slowing or stopping, you should use both brakes:

options.text: Only if the pavement is wet.
Only when riding in the city.

questions.explanation: Using both the front and rear brakes gives you the most stopping power. Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Convex mirrors make cars seem:
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors are curved and show a wider view of the road than flat mirrors. However, they make objects look farther away than they really are.

questions.question: Approved helmets:

options.text: Can limit the view of the motorcycle operator.
Allow the motorcycle operator to see as far to the sides as needed.
Do not have to be worn if the motorcycle operator thinks their view would be limited.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow the motorcycle operator to see as far to the sides as needed.
questions.explanation: Some people worry that helmets limit their vision. This is not true. Approved helmets let you see as far to the sides as you need for safe riding.

questions.question: Before mounting the motorcycle, your pre-ride inspection should include all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your tires, oil, fluids, lights, signals, clutch, throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn. Do a thorough pre-ride inspection every time.

questions.question: To help provide space for drivers attempting to merge into your lane from an entrance ramp, you should:

options.text: Merge into the next lane, if possible.
Not worry about it, since they are the ones trying to merge.
Ride on the far left shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge into the next lane, if possible.
questions.explanation: Drivers merging onto the highway may not see your motorcycle. Move into a different lane if you can to give them plenty of space to merge safely.

questions.question: If your front tire goes flat while you are riding:

options.text: There will be no change in the steering.
The ride will feel too smooth.

questions.explanation: A flat front tire makes steering feel heavy. If your steering feels heavy, pull off the road right away and check your tires.

questions.question: When riding downhill on a motorcycle with a sidecar:

options.text: Stopping will be easier than when riding without a sidecar.
Stopping will take longer than when riding without a sidecar.
Stopping is about as easy as it is when riding without the sidecar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stopping will take longer than when riding without a sidecar.
questions.explanation: A sidecar adds weight to your motorcycle, which means you need more braking power to stop. Slowing and stopping take longer with a sidecar, especially on downhill roads.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat and you must brake, you should:

options.text: Apply the brake of the tire that is not flat.
Apply the brake of the tire that is flat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the brake of the tire that is not flat.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat and you must brake, slowly apply the brake of the tire that is not flat (if you are sure which one that is).

questions.question: Which formation keeps a group of riders closest together?
questions.explanation: A staggered formation keeps a group close while giving each rider enough space. Use single-file when taking curves, turning, or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: When being passed, which of the following is NOT a hazard?

options.text: Objects being thrown from other vehicles.

questions.explanation: When being passed, watch out for the passing vehicle's mirrors, wind gusts, and objects thrown from the vehicle. These are all hazards. Headlights are not a hazard when being passed.

questions.question: Your lane position should NOT:

options.text: Increase your ability to see and be seen.
Provide you with an escape route.
Invite other drivers into your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Invite other drivers into your lane.
questions.explanation: Good lane position keeps you out of blind spots, helps you see and be seen, avoids road hazards, avoids wind blasts, and gives you an escape route. Your position should discourage other drivers from sharing your lane.

questions.question: The front brake provides how much of a motorcycle's stopping power?
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides about three-quarters of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle with a sidecar, the passenger should ride:

options.text: Either on the motorcycle or in the sidecar.
Neither on the motorcycle or in the sidecar.

questions.explanation: If your motorcycle has a sidecar, your passenger should ride in the sidecar. They should keep their hands inside the sidecar at all times.

questions.question: To increase your visibility, you should:

options.text: Turn off your headlight during the day.
Keep your headlight on at all times.
Ride in the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your headlight on at all times.
questions.explanation: To be more visible, wear bright and reflective clothing, keep your headlight on all the time, and change your lane position as needed.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, you should:

options.text: Grip the handlebars firmly and slowly release the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the handlebars firmly and slowly release the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up, as this makes the wobble worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly, slow down by gradually releasing the throttle, move your weight forward and down, and pull off the road. Do not brake, as this can also worsen the wobble.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Judge distances the same as during the day.

questions.explanation: When riding at night, reduce your speed and increase your following distance. Use your high beam when there is no other traffic. Be ready to adjust your lane position as conditions change.

questions.question: A danger of braking too hard is:

options.text: Losing grip on one or both wheels.

questions.correctAnswerText: Losing grip on one or both wheels.
questions.explanation: If you brake too hard, you can lose grip on one or both wheels and crash.

questions.question: What can help if your drive chain slips?
questions.explanation: If your chain slips, try tightening it. If tightening does not fix the problem, replace the chain before riding.

questions.question: Your motorcycle is weaving while riding over rain grooves or bridge gratings. What should you do?

options.text: Stay calm, keep your speed steady, and ride straight across.
Grip the handlebars tightly and speed up to get past the hazard.
Ride on the shoulder instead of the grooves.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm, keep your speed steady, and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: Weaving over rain grooves or bridge gratings is not dangerous. Stay calm and ride straight across at a steady speed. Trying to avoid the weaving by zigzagging is more dangerous than riding straight.

questions.question: During your pre-ride inspection, which item should you NOT check?
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your tires, oil, fluid levels, headlight, taillight, turn signals, brake light, clutch, throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn.

questions.question: When braking, what should you do?

options.text: Use only one brake in non-emergency situations.
Use both brakes only when riding on wet pavement.

questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: The body gets rid of one alcoholic drink per hour. If someone drank eight drinks four hours ago, how many drinks are likely still in their body?
questions.explanation: Subtract the hours passed from the total drinks consumed. Eight drinks minus four hours equals about four drinks remaining in the body.

questions.question: When riding at night, which action should you NOT do?

options.text: Use your high beam light, if possible.

questions.explanation: To stay safe at night, reduce your speed and increase your following distance. Use headlights of other vehicles to see ahead. Use your high beam headlight, except when following or meeting another vehicle.
